'''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月讀宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Nakamura Town, [[:en:Ise City|Ise City]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}} (Naikū) auxiliary shrine of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingū]]. It is also listed as a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}. In some instances, it is written with the simplified characters as "月'''読'''宮."

During the 62nd [[Jingū Shikinen Sengū|Shikinen Sengu]] of Ise Jingū, the {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御|qid=Q24892914}} ceremony was held approximately one year after the Naikū’s own ceremony, taking place on {{ill|October 6|ab|Жьҭаарамза 6|af|6 Oktober|als|6. == Overview ==
[[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the Main Approach Entrance]]
[[File:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qid=Q17191305}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine]]
[[File:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Chozuya and Shukueiya]]

'''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' is an auxiliary shrine ({{ill|Setsumatsusha|ja|別宮|lt=Betsugū}}) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine), located in Nakamura Town along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|en|Isuzu River|qid=Q6089522|lt=Isuzu River}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from Kōtai Jingū. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|en|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi}} (Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto). It is also affectionately called "'''Tsukiyomi-san'''." The deity {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} at the Outer Shrine, which is also referred to as "Tsukiyomi-san," is considered to be the same deity.

Within the shrine precincts are three other auxiliary shrines:
* '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya}}''', enshrining the spirit of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto
* '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto)
* '''{{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya}}''', enshrining {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qid=Q682306|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q682306}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto)

Apart from {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|qid=Q11566292}}, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings. Although these shrines are smaller in scale compared to the main shrine, the four {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|es|Shinmeizukuri|fr|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|ru|Симмэй-дзукури|tr|Shinmei-zukuri|zh|神明造|qid=Q930545|lt=Shimmei-zukuri}}-style shrine buildings standing side by side are an impressive sight. The relocation ceremonies ({{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}) for Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya took place on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya on October 10, 2014.<ref name="ik1410"/> The old timber from Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, dismantled in 2014, was donated to {{ill|Yagumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|qid=Q11391850}}, in Midoricho, Ashikaga City, Tochigi Prefecture, which had lost its main hall to a fire in 2012.<ref name="yu1502">{{Cite web|lang=ja|url=http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|title=八雲神社に待望の本殿 伊勢神宮が譲渡|date=2015-02-21|accessdate=2015-02-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228134757/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/tochigi/news/20150220-OYTNT50379.html|archivedate=2015-02-28}}</ref>

From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya. However, the proper order of worship is Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya, Isanagi-no-Miya, and Isanami-no-Miya.

Since Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the enshrined deity, is the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, the highest deity, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya holds the second highest Rank among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|es|Aramatsuri no miya|fr|Aramatsuri no miya|ja|荒祭宮|qid=Q2859485}}, which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu. Among the auxiliary shrines outside the precincts of the Inner Shrine, it holds the highest Rank.

Besides the four auxiliary shrines mentioned above, the precinct also houses the auxiliary shrine '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qid=Q17191305}}'''. Similar to other auxiliary shrines located outside the main precincts, there is a {{ill|Shukueiya|ja|宿衛屋}} where shrine staff are stationed during visiting hours to distribute talismans and amulets, and to assist with rituals and offerings.

== {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神}} ==
* [[Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto]]<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/| title=月読宮（皇大神宮別宮）| accessdate=2024-03-09}}</ref>

== History ==
The origins are unclear, but according to the Daijingu Gishikichō (大神宮儀式帳) from Enryaku 23 (804) during the reign of the 50th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|en|Emperor Kanmu|qid=Q314846|lt=Kanmu}}, it is recorded that "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya consisted of one complex with four main halls" (月讀宮一院、正殿四区), all enshrined within a single sacred fence (mizugaki). At that time, the four associated shrines were collectively referred to as "Tsukiyomi-no-Miya." 

In Jōgan 9 (867), during the reign of the 56th emperor, {{ill|Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa}}, the shrines {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya}} were officially granted their shrine titles.

According to the Engishiki (延喜式) from Enchō 5 (927) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Daigo|en|Emperor Daigo|qid=Q329753|lt=Daigo}}, at that time, Isanagi-no-Miya and Isanami-no-Miya were enclosed within a single sacred fence as one complex, while Tsukiyomi-no-Miya and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)|ja|月讀荒御魂宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Aramitama)}} also formed a single complex.

Since 1873 (Meiji 6), all four shrines have had their own separate sacred fences, forming the current structure.

== Festivals ==

Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, and offerings of heihaku (幣帛), sacred cloth or objects, are presented by the Imperial Household during major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai.

* January
** {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}} (歳旦祭) (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the Imperial throne.
** {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}} (January 3): A ceremony to mark the beginning of the year, celebrating the origins of the Imperial succession (Amatsu Hitsuji).

* February
** Kenkoku [[Kinensai|Kinen-sai]] (建国記念祭) (February 11): A festival commemorating the founding of the nation and honoring {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} as the mythical first emperor of Japan.
** {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}} (February 18): A festival held at the beginning of the year to pray for a bountiful harvest and the peace of the nation.
** Tenchō-sai (天長祭) (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Naruhito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳仁|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q217096}}.

* May
** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (May 14): Rituals are conducted at the Outer and Inner Shrines, as well as at associated shrines, offering heihaku to pray for protection against natural disasters like storms and for a good harvest.

* June
** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|en:draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (June 18–19): Held in June and December to pray for the peace of the nation and the longevity of the Emperor. Along with the Kannamesai, it is one of the Sansetsu-sai or Sanji-sai (Three Major Festivals) at the shrine.

* August
** Kazahinomi-sai (風日祈祭) (August 4): Similar to the May festival, this ritual involves offering heihaku at the Outer and Inner Shrines, praying for protection against wind and rain, and for agricultural prosperity.

* October
** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai Festival}} (October 18–19): A key harvest festival where priests offer newly harvested crops as sacred food offerings (Ōmike - 大御饌) to the deities, expressing gratitude for the year's bounty.

* November
** {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}} (November 24): A festival where the Emperor offers newly harvested rice to the gods and partakes of it himself, expressing thanks for the harvest.

* December
** {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|en:draft|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|lt=Tsukinami-sai}} (月次祭) (December 18–19): Similar to the June Tsukinami-sai, held to ensure national peace and the Emperor's prosperity.

== Shrine Grounds ==

The shrine buildings of the four Betsugū (別宮, auxiliary shrines) are nearly identical, following the architectural style of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}} (the Inner Shrine), regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female. They feature the Shinmei-zukuri style with thatched roofs, inward-facing chigi (千木) and an even number of six katsuogi (鰹木). The Kodenchi (古殿地), or site of the previous shrine used during the Shikinen Sengū (式年遷宮, ritual reconstruction), is usually adjacent to the new shrine from east to west, but for Tsukiyomi-no-Miya, the sites are aligned north to south and are not directly adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii gate is also larger.

* {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}}
** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine).  
** The highest-Ranking Betsugū located outside the Inner Shrine precincts.

* {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Aramitama-no-Miya}}
** Enshrined deity: Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto Aramitama (月讀尊荒御魂), the wild/spiritual aspect of Tsukiyomi.
** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine.

* {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanagi-no-Miya}}
** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} (Izanagi-no-Mikoto).  
** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine.

* {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naiku)|ja|月讀宮|es|Tsukiyomi no miya (Naikū)|lt=Izanami-no-Miya}}
** Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊弉冉尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qid=Q682306|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q682306}} (Izanami-no-Mikoto).  
** Auxiliary shrine (Betsugū) of the Inner Shrine.

* {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qid=Q17191305}}  
** Enshrined Deities:  
***  Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (佐佐津比古命)  
***  Ukanomitama-no-Mioya-no-Mikoto (宇加乃御玉御祖命)  
***  Ikari-hime-no-Mikoto (伊加利比売命)  
** These deities are regarded as gods of agriculture, protecting rice fields and crops.  
** 末社 (Massha, subordinate shrine) of the Inner Shrine.
** Similar to the Inner Shrine, Ashihara Shrine features Shinmei-zukuri architecture with inward-facing chigi and an even number of four katsuogi, with board roofing.

* Shukueiya (宿衛屋)  
** The Shukueiya serves as the shrine office where priests are stationed during visiting hours to manage rituals, distribute amulets, and assist with offerings and kagura performances.

== Access ==

* Nearest Train Station:  
** Approximately 10 minutes on foot south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|en|Isuzugawa Station|qid=Q6089533|lt=Isuzugawa Station}} on the {{ill|Kintetsu Toba Line|ja|Toba Line}} operated by {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|en|Kintetsu Railway|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu Railway}}.  
** About 1 hour on foot from {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=JR Sangū Line}} operated by {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|ckb|کۆمپانیای ناوەڕاستی ڕێگای ئاسنینی ژاپۆن|cs|JR Central|da|Central Japan Railway Company|de|Central Japan Railway Company|eo|JR Centra|es|Central Japan Railway Company|fa|شرکت راه‌آهن مرکزی ژاپن|fi|JR Tōkai|fr|Central Japan Railway Company|hu|Central Japan Railway Company|id|Perusahaan Kereta Api Jepang Tengah|it|Central Japan Railway Company|ja|東海旅客鉄道|jv|Central Japan Railway Company|ko|도카이 여객철도|ms|Syarikat Kereta Api Jepun Tengah|nds|JR Tōkai|nl|Central Japan Railway Company|pl|Central Japan Railway Company|pt|Central Japan Railway Company|ru|Central Japan Railway Company|su|Pausahaan Japan Railway Tengah|sv|JR Tokai|th|บริษัทรถไฟญี่ปุ่นตอนกลาง|tl|Central Japan Railway Company|tr|Central Japan Railway Company|uk|Central Japan Railway Company|ur|سنٹرل جاپان ریلوے کمپنی|wuu|东海旅客铁道|zh|東海旅客鐵道|zh_yue|東海旅客鐵道|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central}}.

* Nearest Bus Stop:  
** About 5 minutes on foot from Nakamura-cho Bus Stop served by the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} Route 51 (Gekū-Naikū Line).

* Nearest Expressway Interchange:  
** Approximately 1 km from the {{ill|Ise interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884857}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|en|Ise Expressway|qid=Q6079578|lt=Ise Expressway}}.

* Main Roads:  
** Located along the {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 37 (Toba-Matsusaka Line)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357923}} (Miyuki Road) at the front approach entrance.
** Accessible via {{ill|Japan National Route 23|en|Japan National Route 23|qid=Q5357579|lt=National Route 23 (Japan)}} at the rear approach entrance.

* Parking:  
** A large parking lot suitable for buses is available on the National Route 23 side.  
** There are also a few parking spaces available on the prefectural road side.

'''Tsukiyomi-no-miya''' (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine located in Nakamura-chō, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ar|إيسه|azb|ایسه، میه|bcl|Ise, Mie|be|Ісэ (горад)|ca|Ise (ciutat japonesa)|ce|Исе (гӀала)|ckb|ئیسێ|cs|Ise (Mie)|de|Ise (Mie)|eo|Ise (urbo)|es|Ise (Mie)|et|Ise (Jaapan)|eu|Ise (Mie)|fa|ایسه، میه|fi|Ise (kaupunki)|fr|Ise (Mie)|gl|Ise|hr|Ise|hy|Իսե (քաղաք)|id|Ise, Mie|it|Ise (Giappone)|ja|伊勢市|ka|ისე|ko|이세시|lt|Isė (Japonija)|mg|Ise|mzn|ایسه، میه|nl|Ise (Mie)|no|Ise (Mie)|pl|Ise (Japonia)|pt|Ise (Japão)|ro|Ise, Japonia|ru|Исе (город)|sh|Ise|simple|Ise, Mie|sr|Исе|sv|Ise, Japan|szl|Ise (Japůńijo)|tg|Исе|tl|Ise, Mie|tr|Ise (şehir)|tt|Исе (шәһәр)|uk|Ісе (Міє)|ur|ایسے، میہ|uz|Ise (Mie)|vi|Ise, Mie|war|Ise, Mie|zh|伊勢市|zh_classical|伊勢市|zh_min_nan|Ise-chhī|zh_yue|伊勢|qid=Q328067}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}. It is an auxiliary shrine (betsugū) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. It is sometimes written with the abbreviated characters “月読宮”.

=== Enshrined deities ===
{{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt='''Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto'''}}<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ise-kanko.jp/purpose/tsukiyominomiya1/ |title=Tsukiyomi-no-miya (Auxiliary Shrine of the Inner Shrine) |accessdate=2024-03-09}}</ref> (つきよみのみこと) – the second worship hall from the right when facing Tsukiyomi-no-miya.

'''{{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama}}''' – the rightmost worship hall when facing Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya.

'''{{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}''' – the third worship hall from the right when facing Isanagi-no-miya.

'''{{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}''' – the leftmost worship hall when facing Isanami-no-miya.

=== Overview ===
[[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 09.jpg|thumb|200px|Torii at the main approach entrance]]
[[Image:Ashihara-jinja 01.jpg|thumb|200px|{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qid=Q17191305}}, a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine]]
[[Image:Tukiyomi-no-miya(naiku) 08.jpg|thumb|200px|Temizuya and guardhouse]]
Tsukiyomi-no-miya is an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine located in Nakamura-chō along the middle reaches of the {{ill|Isuzu River|Q6089522|qid=Q6089522}}, about 3.8 km from {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine) and about 1.8 km from {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine). The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}. It is also affectionately called “Tsukiyomi-san”; however, the enshrined deity “Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto” of {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|Q11516023|qid=Q11516023}}, an auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine also called “Tsukiyomi-san,” is considered the same deity as that of the main auxiliary shrine.

Within the precincts are three other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine: '''Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya''', which enshrines the aramitama (rough spirit) of Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto; '''Isanagi-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; and '''Isanami-no-miya''', which enshrines {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}. Aside from Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the only other auxiliary shrine with multiple shrine buildings lined up is {{ill|Takihara-no-Miya|ja|瀧原宮|qid=Q11566292}}, which has two. The shrine buildings are comparable in scale to other auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine except {{ill|Aramatsuri-no-Miya|es|Aramatsuri no miya|fr|Aramatsuri no miya|ja|荒祭宮|qid=Q2859485}}; though smaller than the main sanctuary, the sight of four {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|es|Shinmeizukuri|fr|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|ru|Симмэй-дзукури|tr|Shinmei-zukuri|zh|神明造|qid=Q930545}} shrine buildings standing in a row is magnificent. The transfer ceremonies were held for Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya at 10:00 p.m. on October 6, 2014, and for Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya on {{ill|October 10|Q2921|qid=Q2921}}<ref name="ik1410"/>. Old timbers from Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, dismantled in 2014, were donated to {{ill|Yagumo Shrine|ja|八雲神社 (足利市)|qid=Q11391850|lt=Yakumo Shrine}} in Midori-chō, {{ill|Ashikaga, From right (east) to left, the shrines are arranged as Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya, Tsukiyomi-no-miya, Isanagi-no-miya, and Isanami-no-miya; however, the correct order of worship is said to be Tsukiyomi-no-miya → Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya → Isanagi-no-miya → Isanami-no-miya.

Because Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, the younger sibling deity of the supreme deity {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, is enshrined here, Tsukiyomi-no-miya ranks second among the auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine after '''Aramatsuri-no-miya''', which enshrines the spirit of Amaterasu Ōmikami, and it is the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine’s main precinct.

In addition to the four auxiliary shrines above, the precincts include '''{{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qid=Q17191305}}''', a subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. As with other off-site auxiliary shrines, there is a guardhouse (shukueiya) staffed by priests during visiting hours, where talismans and amulets are bestowed and arrangements are made for kagura dances and food offerings.

=== History ===
Although the exact origins are unclear, the “Daijingū Gishikichō” records that in {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 23 ({{ill|804|Q29998|qid=Q29998}}) during the reign of the 50th emperor {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|Q314846|qid=Q314846}}, “Tsukiyomi-no-miya, one compound, four main sanctuaries” were enshrined within a single sacred fence, and the four auxiliary shrines together were called “Tsukiyomi-no-miya.” In {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 9 ({{ill|867|Q30347|qid=Q30347}}) during the reign of the 56th emperor {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|Q349243|qid=Q349243}}, the shrine names Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya were granted.

According to the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) during the reign of the 60th emperor {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}}, at that time Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya formed one compound enclosed by a sacred fence, and likewise Tsukiyomi-no-miya and Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya formed another. From {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6), all four shrines came to have their own individual sacred fences, forming the current layout.

=== Festivals ===
Rituals are conducted in accordance with those of the Inner Shrine, and for major festivals such as the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings (heihaku) are presented from the Imperial Household.

* January
** Saitansai (January 1): A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial line.
** {{ill|Genshi-sai|Q11387821|qid=Q11387821}} (January 3): A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year.

* February
** National Foundation Commemoration Festival (February 11): A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}.
** {{ill|Kinensai|Q118906710|qid=Q118906710}} (February 18): A festival praying for a bountiful harvest and national peace at the beginning of the year.
** Tenchōsai (February 23): A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Naruhito}}.

* May
** Kazahinomisai (May 14): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests.

* June
** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19): A festival held in June and December praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at Ise Grand Shrine it is, together with the Kannamesai, called one of the Three Seasonal Festivals.

* August
** Kazahinomisai (August 4): A ritual in which offerings are presented to the Outer and Inner Shrines as well as auxiliary and subsidiary shrines, praying for freedom from wind and rain disasters and for abundant harvests.

* October
** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045}} (October 18–19): A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain of the year as sacred food ({{ill|Shinsen|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045|lt=Ōmike}}).

* November
** {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}} (November 24): A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the deities and partakes of it himself, giving thanks for the harvest.

* December
** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19)

=== Precincts ===
[[Image:Tsukiyomi-no-miya(Naiku)_05.JPG|thumb|200px|Isanagi-no-miya and Isanami-no-miya]]
The shrine buildings of the four auxiliary shrines are nearly identical and, regardless of whether the enshrined deity is male or female, follow the Inner Shrine style: thatched Shinmei-zukuri facing south, with inward-cut chigi and an even number (six) of katsuogi. The old shrine sites for periodic rebuilding are usually adjacent east–west, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya they are arranged north–south and are not adjacent. The shrine building of Tsukiyomi-no-miya is slightly larger than the other three, and its torii is also larger.

* Tsukiyomi-no-miya – Auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine); the highest-ranking auxiliary shrine located outside the Inner Shrine precinct.
* Tsukiyomi Aramitama-no-miya – Enshrined deity: Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto no Aramitama; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine.
* Isanagi-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine.
* Isanami-no-miya – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}}; auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine.
* {{ill|Ashihara Shrine|ja|葭原神社|qid=Q17191305}} – Enshrined deities: Sasatsuhiko-no-Mikoto, {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama no Mionoya no Mikoto}}, and Ikarihime-no-Mikoto; all are considered deities of the five grains who protect fields and paddies. A subsidiary shrine of the Inner Shrine. Ashihara Shrine follows the Inner Shrine style, with inward-cut chigi and four (even-numbered) katsuogi, in a board-roofed Shinmei-zukuri style.
* Guardhouse

=== Access ===
* Nearest station: About a 10-minute walk south from {{ill|Isuzugawa Station|Q6089533|qid=Q6089533}} on the {{ill|Toba Line|Q5357612|qid=Q5357612}} of {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085}}
:: About a 1-hour walk from {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023}} of {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|ckb|کۆمپانیای ناوەڕاستی ڕێگای ئاسنینی ژاپۆن|cs|JR Central|da|Central Japan Railway Company|de|Central Japan Railway Company|eo|JR Centra|es|Central Japan Railway Company|fa|شرکت راه‌آهن مرکزی ژاپن|fi|JR Tōkai|fr|Central Japan Railway Company|hu|Central Japan Railway Company|id|Perusahaan Kereta Api Jepang Tengah|it|Central Japan Railway Company|ja|東海旅客鉄道|jv|Central Japan Railway Company|ko|도카이 여객철도|ms|Syarikat Kereta Api Jepun Tengah|nds|JR Tōkai|nl|Central Japan Railway Company|pl|Central Japan Railway Company|pt|Central Japan Railway Company|ru|Central Japan Railway Company|su|Pausahaan Japan Railway Tengah|sv|JR Tokai|th|บริษัทรถไฟญี่ปุ่นตอนกลาง|tl|Central Japan Railway Company|tr|Central Japan Railway Company|uk|Central Japan Railway Company|ur|سنٹرل جاپان ریلوے کمپنی|wuu|东海旅客铁道|zh|東海旅客鐵道|zh_yue|東海旅客鐵道|qid=Q513679}}
* Nearest bus stop: About a 5-minute walk from Nakamura-chō bus stop on the 51 Outer–Inner Shrine Line of {{ill|Mie Kotsu|Q6843516|qid=Q6843516}} ({{ill|Mie Kōtsū Ise Office|Q11357667|qid=Q11357667}})
* Nearest interchange: About 1 km from {{ill|Ise interchange|Q10884857|qid=Q10884857}} on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|Q6079578|qid=Q6079578}}
* Roads: Along {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|Q11357923|qid=Q11357923}} ({{ill|Miyuki Road|Q22222736|qid=Q22222736}}) (main approach), and along {{ill|Japan National Route 23|Q5357579|qid=Q5357579}} (rear approach)
* Parking: There is a large parking lot on the national road side that can accommodate buses; several cars can also be parked on the prefectural road side.
